language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.
language.lessonRating: How do you feel about this exercise?

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
G-day! My name is Becca. This is my grandparent's sheep farm. My grandparents have many sheep on their farm.
Look! There are 1386 sheep grazing on the fresh grass.
There are 2954 sheep grazing on the hillside.
You can make many different numbers from 2, 9, 5, and 4.
When you arrange the four numerals in descending order, that is, 9, 5, 4, 2, you get the largest number you can make,
because all the other numbers are smaller, such as 9452, 5492, and 2459.
When you arrange the four numerals in ascending order, that is, 2, 4, 5, 9, you get the smallest number you can make,
because all other numbers are larger, such as 2549, 4529, and 5942.
What about the second largest number? You can get that by switching the last two digits of the largest number,
that is, 9, 5, 2, 4. It is smaller than 9542, but bigger than all the other numbers.
What about the second smallest number? Right, just switch the last two digits of the smallest number,
that is, 2, 4, 9, 5. Its bigger than 2459, but smaller than all the other numbers
Let’s have more fun counting the sheep!
